title: Canonical radical reader adoption and promotion kit

sourceRefs.summary: Run-contract target that explains why this generated contract exists.
User-approved exact 20-slice radical reader adoption and promotion-kit proposal with a mandatory slice-15 browser checkpoint.

expectedLearning: Whether the released canonical construction and renderer session adopt a structurally distinct radical transition without a new runtime, lifecycle, scheduler, or notation-specific geometry category.
Whether a promotion kit extracted only after fraction and radical evidence reduces the next unit-exponent adoption to content, descriptor wiring, and focused verification.
allowedWork: One radical succession reader-transition adoption through the released canonical equation session.
Generic selector annotation, structural binding, lifecycle, endpoint, and promotion-kit work demonstrated by both the fraction and radical exemplars.
Focused lesson, descriptor, compiler, reader, accessibility, export, browser, performance, and production verification required by the approved exemplar.
The stable visual command and disposable browser review outputs needed for the mandatory slice-15 human checkpoint.
Exact project-memory and Theseus evidence updates required by the approved contract.
disallowedWork: No second renderer, material layer, animation runtime, clock, semantic artifact, or product route.
No radical, glyph, character, KaTeX-class, viewport, route, or operation-specific geometry or scheduling corrections.
No broad radical-family rollout or migration of another product reader family.
No LLM-authored mathematics, DOM, HTML, selectors, geometry, keyframes, timing, typography, accessibility markup, or export code.
No foldable distribution implementation, arithmetic, vector, matrix, derivative, integral, publication-platform, atlas, or unrelated UI work.
No broad utility extraction without identical authority, lifetime, error, and security contracts.
No automatic continuation beyond slice 15 without fresh user approval of the visible browser exemplar.
goal: Adopt one radical succession reader transition through the released canonical construction path, preserve the reader and native semantic contracts, and extract a promotion kit proved by a no-product-route unit-exponent dry run.
commitCadence: Commit every independently reversible verified slice with exact path staging and its completed Theseus evidence.
stopConditions: Stop if any frame has simultaneous compatibility and canonical paint, false semantic identity, fading for structural fusion or fission, or a lifecycle gap.

Stop if the exemplar needs notation-specific geometry, a new lifecycle or scheduler category, a second runtime or clock, or mutation of native settled mathematics, typography, accessibility, or semantic DOM.
Stop if direct seek, rewind, reduced motion, static output, responsive composition, accessibility, export, route budgets, or production closure fails without one bounded generic repair.
Stop at HUMAN_CHECKPOINT after slice 15 for user browser review; this checkpoint is not waived.

After checkpoint approval, stop at slice 18 if the unit-exponent dry run changes compositor core, adds a lifecycle or scheduler category, adds notation-specific geometry, or creates a second runtime artifact.
Stop if work touches unrelated dirty-worktree changes, deferred domains, or exceeds the preservation and rollback boundaries.
Stop if context cannot safely complete and record the remaining contract.
